'''Albert Abramovich Muchnik''' (2 January 1934 – 14 February 2019) was a [[Russian people|Russian]] [[mathematician]] who worked in the field of foundations and [[mathematical logic]].

==Biography==
He received his Ph.D. from [[Moscow State Pedagogical Institute]] in 1959 under the advisorship of [[Pyotr Novikov]]. From there, he wrote his dissertation titled ''Solution to the Post Reducibility Problem.''<ref>[http://genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=113668 Albert Abramovich Muchnik], [[Mathematics Genealogy Project]]. Accessed January 26, 2010</ref> Muchnik's most significant contribution was on the subject of [[relative computability]]. He and [[Richard M. Friedberg|Richard Friedberg]] independently introduced the priority method which gave an affirmative answer to [[Post's problem]] regarding the existence of [[recursively enumerable]] [[Turing degrees]] between ''' 0 ''' and ''' 0' '''. This result, now known as the [[Friedberg–Muchnik theorem]],<ref>Robert I. Soare, [https://books.google.com/books?id=9I7Pl00LU5gC&dq=%22Friedberg-Muchnik+theorem%22&pg=PA118 Recursively Enumberable Sets and Degrees: A Study of Computable Functions and Computably Generated Sets.] [[Springer-Verlag]], 1999, {{ISBN|3-540-15299-7}}; p. 118</ref><ref>Nikolai  Vereshchagin, Alexander Shen, [https://books.google.com/books?id=A6uvsks0abgC&dq=%22Friedberg-Muchnik+theorem%22&pg=PA85 Computable functions.] [[American Mathematical Society]], 2003, {{ISBN|0-8218-2732-4}}; p. 85</ref> opened study of the Turing degrees of the recursively enumerable sets which turned out to possess a very complicated and non-trivial structure.

Muchnik also made significant contributions to Medvedev's theory of mass problems, introducing a generalisation of Turing degrees, called "Muchnik degrees", in 1963.<ref>A. A. Muchnik, ''On strong and weak reducibility of algorithmic problems''. (Russian) 
[[Siberian Mathematical Journal]], vol. 4 (1963), pp. 1328&ndash;1341</ref> Muchnik also elaborated [[Kolmogorov]]'s proposal of viewing [[intuitionism]] as "calculus of problems" and proved that the lattice of Muchnik degrees is [[Intuitionism|Brouwerian]].

Muchnik was married to the Russian mathematician Nadezhda Ermolaeva. Their son [[Andrey Muchnik]], who died in 2007, was also a mathematician working in foundations of mathematics.<ref>S. I. Adian, A. L. Semenov, V. A. Uspenskii, [https://elibrary.ru/item.asp?id=9555845 ''Andrei Albertovich Muchnik''],{{in lang|ru}}  [[Uspekhi Matematicheskikh Nauk]], vol. 62 (2007), no. 4, pp. 140&ndash;144</ref> Albert Muchnik died in February 2019.
